ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs (natural persons controlling ≥25%) and senior managers against the UN Consolidated Security Council Sanctions List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List. PEP status is defined by Article 32 of Law 10/2010 and EU Directive 2018/843. Standard due diligence applies to this Low_Risk_Standard import entity; suspicious transaction reports (ROS) must be filed with SEPBLAC; documentation must be retained for 10 years; UBO register information must be updated annually or upon any change.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (www.rmc.es) with online payment via Colegio de Registradores de España (www.registradores.org) - Negative Denomination Certificate service
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be expressed in Latin script; Spanish (Castilian) is the default statutory language. Names in other Latin-script European languages are admissible if not misleading. Non-Latin scripts (Cyrillic, Arabic, Chinese) must be transliterated into Latin characters according to official Spanish transliteration rules. The denomination must not be identical to any existing registered name and must not mislead as to the company's nature or corporate form.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The negative denomination certificate is valid for 180 days from issuance and may be extended once for an additional 180 days prior to expiry if incorporation has not yet been recorded (Articles 425-426 of Royal Decree 1784/1996, Mercantile Registry Regulation). Upon rejection due to identical or confusing similarity with an existing name, the applicant may (i) immediately file a new application for a distinct denomination without additional formalism, or (ii) within one month of notification, file an administrative appeal (recurso de alzada) to the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública of the Ministry of Justice; the absence of an express resolution within three months constitutes a negative administrative silence.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual and serviced offices are accepted for the registered office of a Spanish S.L. provided the address is a real, locatable place where the administration is in fact based or where the principal activity is conducted, and where the tax authority (AEAT) and Mercantile Registry can serve effective notices. For an ISIC 4632 frozen meat/seafood import wholesaler, the registered office may be virtual for corporate purposes, but the operational cold-chain activity requires a separate physically registered establishment under the Registro General Sanitario de Empresas Alimentarias y Alimentos (RGSEAA) and compliance with customs sanitary inspection regimes.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Unannounced physical inspection of the registered office by AEAT or the Mercantile Registry in the first fiscal year is low (approximately 15%). Customs and sanitary inspection of imported frozen beef and seafood at point of entry is nearly certain (95-100%) per EU official controls under Regulation (EU) 2017/625. Periodic sanitary inspection of the licensed cold storage facility by the competent autonomous community health authority is moderate (approximately 30% in the first operational year).

To subscribe to the share capital of the Company in the total amount of EUR 3,000, representing 100% of the subscribed capital, to be paid in full upon incorporation. 2. national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), including its electronic headquarters at sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es. The Spanish Tax Identification Number (NIF) is the principal statutory tax identifier. The Spanish VAT identification number is the NIF prefixed by ES for intra-Community transactions and VIES registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada must obtain an NIF from the AEAT by filing Modelo 036, normally before commencing economic activity, making taxable supplies, acquiring assets, or entering into relevant tax relationships. A provisional NIF may be issued during incorporation and must be converted into a definitive NIF after registration with the Commercial Registry and submission of the registered deed and supporting corporate documents. The application generally requires the incorporation deed or draft deed, Commercial Registry evidence where available, registered office evidence, identification of directors and authorized representatives, and powers of attorney where applicable. Non-resident directors, shareholders, and representatives generally require a Spanish NIE or other accepted identification. The company must register its business activities and tax obligations through Modelo 036. A VAT number for intra-Community operations is requested through Modelo 036 and inclusion in the Registro de Operadores Intracomunitarios; activation is subject to AEAT verification. An EORI number must be obtained from the customs authorities for importing or exporting goods. Import VAT is generally accounted for through customs declarations, with optional postponed import VAT accounting available to qualifying businesses that elect it within the applicable Spanish VAT-registration framework.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A Spanish SL is ordinarily subject to Spanish Corporate Income Tax as a separate legal person. Spain does not provide a general United States-style check-the-box election for an SL. Tax transparency regimes apply only to specifically regulated vehicles and circumstances and are not the default treatment for an SL. A Spanish tax group regime may be available where statutory ownership, control, and other requirements are met; it is an optional consolidated Corporate Income Tax regime rather than an entity-classification election. A VAT group regime may also be available to qualifying closely linked entities, subject to statutory conditions and formal election. Spain has anti-hybrid mismatch rules implementing EU ATAD requirements; these operate as mandatory limitation or denial rules and are not elective classification mechanisms.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido, IVA), harmonized with the EU VAT Directive. Mainland Spain and the Balearic Islands are within the Spanish VAT territory. The Canary Islands, Ceuta, and Melilla are outside Spanish VAT territory and have separate indirect tax systems.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general turnover threshold applies for Spanish VAT registration. A taxable person must register before commencing an economic activity or making transactions giving rise to VAT obligations, irrespective of turnover. Certain transactions are exempt, outside scope, or subject to special regimes, but they do not create a general small-business registration threshold for an importing wholesale SL.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Invoices must comply with Spanish VAT invoicing rules, including sequential numbering, date, supplier and customer identification, NIF or VAT number where required, description, taxable base, VAT rate, VAT amount, and legally required references. Electronic invoices are permitted subject to authenticity, integrity, legibility, and recipient-acceptance requirements. The Immediate Supply of Information system (Suministro Inmediato de Información, SII) requires qualifying taxpayers, including taxpayers exceeding the statutory large-business turnover threshold, VAT groups, and taxpayers under the monthly refund regime, to transmit specified invoice-record data electronically to the AEAT generally within four calendar days, subject to statutory adjustments. SII is not a universal real-time clearance mandate. Spain is implementing the electronic invoicing and invoice-system requirements under Law 18/2022 and Royal Decree 1007/2023, including the VERI*FACTU framework and future mandatory B2B electronic invoicing; implementation dates depend on the applicable regulatory timetable and taxpayer category. Until the relevant mandate applies, there is no universal requirement for every SL to obtain pre-clearance or a digital tax stamp for each invoice. Customs declarations and import VAT accounting are processed through the Spanish customs electronic systems and the EU customs framework.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.industry_specific_import_notes: Imports of frozen beef and pelagic fish from outside the EU generally trigger customs formalities, customs duty where applicable, import VAT, and food, veterinary, sanitary, and official-control requirements. The importer must normally hold an EORI number and comply with EU customs, animal-health, food-safety, border-control, and traceability rules. Tariff classification, origin, quotas, preferential agreements, sanitary certificates, and Border Control Post procedures may materially affect duty and import clearance. Intra-Community acquisitions are subject to Spanish VAT self-assessment where applicable. Domestic wholesale supplies are generally subject to 21% VAT unless a specific reduced-rate rule applies; the ordinary supply of frozen meat and fish for wholesale trading should not be assumed to qualify for a reduced rate without transaction-specific review.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods dispatched or transported from Spain to a destination outside the EU VAT territory may qualify for VAT exemption with the right to deduct, functionally equivalent to zero-rating, where the statutory export conditions are satisfied and the exporter retains evidence of export. The goods must leave the relevant EU customs territory and the exporter must be able to link the commercial invoice, transport, customs declaration, and customs exit confirmation. Supplies to customers in another EU Member State may qualify for VAT exemption with the right to deduct as an intra-Community supply where the customer has a valid VAT identification number, the goods are transported to another Member State, the supplier reports the transaction correctly, and documentary transport and recapitulative-statement requirements are met. Services supplied to non-EU customers are not automatically zero-rated; their treatment depends on place-of-supply rules, customer status, service type, use-and-enjoyment rules, and applicable exemptions. A VAT refund or repayment requires deductible input VAT, valid invoices or import records, proper VAT-book and return reporting, and absence of exclusionary rules.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic export customs declaration accepted by Spanish customs, normally including the MRN
Electronic confirmation of exit from the EU customs territory or equivalent customs export evidence
Commercial invoice identifying the exporter, consignee, goods, value, delivery terms, and transaction reference
Packing list and transport documentation, such as bill of lading, sea waybill, air waybill, CMR, or equivalent
Import-country customs or delivery evidence where necessary to substantiate destination
For intra-Community supplies: customer VAT identification number, transport evidence, and correct EC Sales List reporting
For frozen beef and fish where applicable: veterinary, sanitary, catch, health, origin, quota, and border-control documentation
Bank payment and accounting records supporting the commercial transaction; an inward remittance certificate is not generally a statutory Spanish VAT export document
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.fx_repatriation_rule: Not applicable. Spain generally has no universal statutory requirement to repatriate export proceeds within 180 days or within another fixed period as a condition for export VAT exemption. Export proceeds remain subject to ordinary accounting, anti-money-laundering, customs, transfer-pricing, financial-reporting, and banking-documentation requirements. A bank, financing arrangement, letter of credit, export-credit policy, or foreign-currency control applicable to a particular transaction may impose separate contractual or operational deadlines.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT may deny export exemption or intra-Community exemption and assess underpaid VAT, late-payment interest, and applicable penalties where export, transport, customer identification, customs exit, or reporting evidence is insufficient. The assessment may include the VAT that should have been charged, statutory interest, and penalties calculated under the Spanish General Tax Law; serious or very serious infringements may attract percentage-based penalties, with increases or reductions depending on concealment, fraudulent means, repeated conduct, conformity, and prompt payment. Incorrect deductions or refund claims may be reversed, with repayment of the refunded amount, interest, and penalties. False invoices, fictitious exports, customs fraud, smuggling, money laundering, or deliberate VAT fraud may create administrative and, where statutory thresholds and intent requirements are met, criminal exposure. Customs debts may also be reassessed for duty, import VAT, interest, and customs penalties. Export documentation must be retained for the applicable Spanish tax limitation and record-retention periods, commonly at least four years for tax assessment purposes, subject to longer periods under accounting, customs, anti-money-laundering, or sector-specific rules.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), acting under the exchange control framework of Royal Decree 664/1999, the EU Treaty provisions on free movement of capital, and the Foreign Exchange Transaction reporting obligations of Royal Decree 304/2014 and Banco de España Circular 4/2012.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain operates as a fully liberalised capital and current account within the European Economic and Monetary Union; the euro is fully convertible, and profit remittance is unrestricted for resident SL entities subject to corporate tax clearance, transfer pricing compliance, and anti-money laundering checks. No general exchange control approval is required for dividends or repatriated capital, but transactions exceeding EUR 100,000 must be declared to the Directorate for Foreign Trade for balance-of-payments statistics; frozen assets or sanctions-related restrictions apply only to designated jurisdictions and persons.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender obligation or mandatory conversion ratio applies to export receipts; export proceeds may be retained in foreign currency or freely sold into euros. However, all export collection operations must be paid through a resident Spanish credit institution within the customary commercial settlement period, and receivables exceeding EUR 50,000 per transaction must be reported to Banco de España via the balance-of-payments declaration system within prescribed monthly reporting calendars.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (current account for trade receivables and payables)
Capital Escrow Account (initial share capital deposit) and Operational Account
Operational Account with dedicated trade finance facility for documentary credits

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banco de España (as registrar of the minimum capital escrow required by the notarial instrument)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Statutory Capital Escrow Account (temporary deposit for SL formation)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Limited and disfavoured as a primary treasury rail. Spain, as an EU Member State, permits licensed electronic money institutions (EMIs) to operate under PSD2 and the EBA passporting regime, but major tier-1 banking counterparties and trade finance providers require a physical licensed bank for documentary collections, commercial letters of credit, and AML-compliant high-volume trade settlement. Offshore EMIs without an EU banking licence or MiFID authorisation cannot issue commercial LCs or provide regulated foreign exchange hedging; feasibility is rated Low for primary clearing, though supplementary use as a payment-only rail is Medium.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of at least one managing director is generally mandatory at the account opening interview for Spanish SLs in tier-1 branches; remote opening through video-identification is legally permissible under Law 10/2010 when using an accredited certification service, but most commercial banks still require notarised powers of attorney and an in-person signatory for the first activation. Beneficial owners and authorised signatories must be available for supplementary due diligence if the operation triggers enhanced review.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: Registered capital for an SL (minimum EUR 3,000) is considered disproportionately low for a wholesale frozen meat and seafood import operation expecting high transaction turnover.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the notarised deed of incorporation, current statutory accounts showing shareholder loan or equity injection, projected cash flow model for Year 1, signed commercial contracts or purchase orders with international suppliers, and a board resolution endorsing the treasury plan.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: Non-resident ownership and inbound share capital from entities domiciled in high-risk or Latin American jurisdictions with opaque beneficial ownership.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit a complete corporate ownership chart identifying all ultimate beneficial owners with certified passports, recent utility or government-issued proof of address, audited financial statements of the shareholder, professional references from the foreign bank, and legalisation or apostilles on corporate registry extracts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: Trade-based AML red flags arising from high-volume documentary LCs for frozen beef carcasses and pelagic fish with price variances against commodity benchmarks.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Maintain a trade file containing third-party scanned ocean bills of lading, customs import declarations to Spain (DUA/TARIC), quality and phytosanitary certificates, freezing chamber inspection logs, supplier export licences, and an independent commodity price benchmark report (e.g., Mintec or Mercabarna quotations) for each shipment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: Sanctions screening hits associated with seafood supply chains transiting or sourcing from countries with partial embargo regimes or ports under secondary sanctions pressure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Hold an export compliance dossier with end-to-end vessel tracking evidence, letter of non-interest from the supplier, US/EU/OFAC and EU Financial Sanctions Database screening results for all vessels and counterparties, import permits from the Spanish Ministry of Agriculture or health authorities, and a written attestation from the logistics provider confirming no unauthorised transshipment.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity capital injections should be wired from the foreign parent or lender via SWIFT MT103 in EUR or convertible USD, with beneficiary account named ES_SL at the Spanish bank and purpose code classifying the transfer as 'Foreign Direct Investment (equity)' or 'Intercompany Financing' in the Banco de España balance-of-payments declaration. The Bank of Spain identification code (e.g., DGI number) obtained via the Statutory Registry of Foreign Investments must accompany payments over EUR 100,000; supporting documentation includes the notarial deed, the foreign investment declaration, and, if applicable, the loan agreement and tax form 200 declaration for intra-group financing transparency.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound payments to international frozen beef carcass and pelagic fish suppliers will be routed primarily through SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfer for incumbent suppliers and, for higher-value or first-time transactions, through commercial letters of credit issued under UCP 600 via SWIFT MT700/MT707 and settled through SWIFT MT202/MT202COV. Revolving documentary LC facilities and standby credits are recommended to match the cold-chain import cycle, with P-2 and P-3 clearing in EUR/USD or using TARGET2 for euro leg and CHIPS/Fedwire for USD leg, ensuring two-factor authentication and reconciliation against sanctioned party lists.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright OTC FX forwards (EUR/USD) transacted under ISDA 1992 or ISDA 2002 master agreement with a Spanish credit institution
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on emerging-market currencies (e.g., Brazilian real or Argentine peso) where the import supply chain invoices in a non-deliverable currency
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD) to convert trade loan liabilities or capital injections into the SL functional currency
FX options (European-style) purchased to cap upside exposure on significant LNG or shipping-related USD cost components
FX rolling forwards or window forwards aligned with the 30–90 day cold-chain settlement calendar

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the end of the financial year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines of €1,500 to €3,000 per month of delay; potential administrative strike-off after 2 years of non-compliance

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit if the company exceeds two of the following thresholds: total assets exceeding €2,000,000; net turnover exceeding €4,000,000; average number of employees exceeding 50
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish General Accounting Plan (Plan General de Contabilidad), aligned with IFRS

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual confirmation of beneficial ownership required for shareholding transfers; updates notified to the registry within one month of changes

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: General 25% corporate income tax rate; newly created SL qualifies for a reduced 15% rate on the first EUR 300,000 of taxable base for its first two tax periods with positive taxable base (Art. 29 Law 27/2014). Participation exemption relief (95%-100%) may apply to qualifying foreign dividends and capital gains. Foreign tax credit relief is available for taxes paid abroad on income sourced outside Spain. No sector-specific tax holiday exists for frozen beef and seafood imports.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200 — corporate income tax return filed electronically through the AEAT 'Sede Electrónica' (www.agenciatributaria.es).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 25 calendar days following the six months after the fiscal year-end; for a 31 December year-end, the deadline is 25 July of the next calendar year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit before corporate income tax (resultado contable antes de impuestos).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Spanish SL must declare its worldwide income. Non-resident shareholders do not file the SL's Form 200; the SL is the sole resident taxpayer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base (base imponible) after adjustments, prior-year loss offset and transfer pricing corrections.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Adjust for arm's length pricing on related-party imports, management fees, royalties, and financing. Attach the transfer pricing documentation package and Form 232 where required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full tax payable (cuota íntegra) applying the 25% statutory rate or the 15% newly created company rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply double tax treaty credits in the subsequent credits section; ensure DTA relief is not incorrectly claimed at Box 553 level.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net tax due after credits, withholdings, and quarterly instalments paid (cuota líquida / resulting payment).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The SL must pay any net tax due by the same deadline. Dividend WHT on distributions to non-resident shareholders is a separate withholding obligation borne by the paying SL and reported in Form 123 / 216.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing without prior tax office request: surcharge of 5% of the outstanding tax for the first month, 10% for the second month, 15% for the third month, and 20% from the fourth month onward. Late filing after a tax office request: 50% surcharge plus default interest. If no tax is payable, a flat penalty of EUR 200 applies. Penalties for inaccurate or incomplete filing may reach 50%-150% of the omitted amount where evasion is involved.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Domestic IRNR withholding rate: 19% for residents of the EU, EEA, or a country with a double tax treaty with Spain; 24% for residents of non-treaty jurisdictions. Dividends paid to a qualifying EU parent may be exempt under the Parent-Subsidiary Directive (holding of at least 10%, minimum 1-year holding period).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply treaty relief, the non-resident shareholder must provide a Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) issued by its competent tax authority to the Spanish paying entity before or at the time of payment. The TRC must be translated into Spanish (unless bilingual), remain valid, certify effective tax residence, and be updated on request. If the full domestic rate is withheld, the shareholder may file a refund claim using Form 211 (IRNR return) or Form 210 within the four-year statutory period, attaching the TRC, evidence of beneficial ownership, shareholding percentage, and holding period. Confirmation may alternatively be requested via the Spanish mutual consultation procedure or advanced DTA clearance from the AEAT.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic statutory rates: interest 19% (EU/EEA/treaty residents) or 24% (non-treaty residents); royalties 19% (EU/EEA/treaty residents) or 24% (non-treaty residents). Under the EU Interest-Royalties Directive, a 0% withholding rate applies to related companies with a direct holding of at least 25% for an uninterrupted 24-month period. Most Spanish tax treaties cap interest at 5%-10% and royalties at 5%-10% depending on the treaty partner.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File obligation arises where related-party transactions with a single related person exceed EUR 250,000 in the tax period. A separate Master File is required where the group's consolidated revenue reaches EUR 750,000,000; Form 232 (related-party transactions information return) is mandatory if the aggregate amount of related-party transactions exceeds EUR 250,000 per related person or EUR 1,000,000 in total.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain applies general substance and anti-abuse principles under the Corporate Income Tax Law and the EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive, not the UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations. For a Spanish SL, incorporation in Spain normally establishes tax residence under Art. 8 Law 27/2014, but actual management, employees, premises, and decision-making must support compliance. Lack of commercial substance can trigger the GAAR (Art. 15 Law 58/2003), CFC attribution, denial of treaty benefits, and refusal of the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption where abuse is found.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Understating import revenues from cold-chain wholesale sales; issuing fictitious invoices; manipulating customs declarations for frozen beef and pelagic fish; using shell companies to hide taxable profit inside Spain.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalty of 50%-150% of the omitted tax plus late-payment interest (Law 58/2003). Criminal tax fraud above EUR 120,000 under Art. 305 of the Spanish Criminal Code carries imprisonment of 1 to 6 years and a fine of up to six times the defrauded amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be jointly and severally liable under Art. 42 Law 58/2003 when they caused or tolerated the fraud. Criminal sanctions may include personal fines, embargoes, travel bans, disqualification, and imprisonment; the corporate veil may be pierced for civil restitution of the defrauded tax.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a Spanish SL with no genuine office, staff, or managerial oversight while booking all sales through Spain and accumulating profits without distributed dividends; or routing purchases via a no-substance intermediary in a low-tax jurisdiction solely to strip margin from the Spanish entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The AEAT may recharacterise or disregard artificial legal transactions under Art. 15 Law 58/2003, reassess the Spanish SL's taxable base, impose a penalty of 25% on the corrected tax base, and deny treaty benefits. CFC rules may attribute Spanish income to the non-resident parent, triggering IRNR or additional corporate tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly operate an artificial structure risk personal exposure for corporate tax adjustments and penalties. In serious cases, tax auditors may apply veil-piercing to reach personal assets; travel bans and director disqualification may follow in criminal proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to benchmark an arm's length margin for the import-distribution function of the Spanish SL; non-submission of Form 232 or the Local File/Master File; mispricing intercompany purchases of frozen beef and seafood so the Spanish entity shows negligible tax profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Mandatory correction of taxable income to arm's length; monetary penalty of 15% of the amount of undocumented related-party transactions (Art. 18.13 Law 27/2014). A EUR 1,000 penalty per data item applies for Form 232 omissions, capped at EUR 15,000. In fraud cases, the penalty can rise to 50%-150% of the added tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for the corporate entity's tax debt if their negligent or intentional pricing conduct caused the under-payment. Serious mispricing may be prosecuted as criminal fraud, leading to personal fines, confiscation, travel restrictions, and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using over-invoicing or under-invoicing on Swift TT or Revolving LC payment rails for frozen beef and seafood to move value across borders; accepting trade finance from undisclosed beneficial owners; dealing with parties subject to EU sanctions; repeatedly structuring payments below recording thresholds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Law 10/2010, serious AML breaches are punished with fines of EUR 60,000 up to EUR 5,000,000 or 5% of net assets, plus public censure and freezing orders. Separcional SEPBLAC enforcement can suspend the entity's activity and impose additional administrative sanctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, beneficial owners, and compliance officers may face direct fines, prohibition on managing companies, travel bans, seizure of personal assets, and criminal prosecution for money laundering under the Spanish Criminal Code. The corporate veil can be pierced if the SL was used as a laundering vehicle.
